title: OwnFrame syndicate
description: Validates one file in data/syndicates/: a single syndicate — its ranks, what each rank-up costs, its alignments and how standing is earned. One file per syndicate, named <id>.json = one wiki page. What the syndicate sells lives in data/vendors/ (vendors point here via `syndicate`), so offers are never kept twice. Alignment percentages are fixed by the game (allied +50 %, opposed -50 %, enemy -100 %) and live in the apps, not here. Write entries from what the game shows — do not copy tables from other wikis.

$schema.description: Optional relative path to this schema, for editor autocompletion.

name.description: Syndicate name as shown in game (English), e.g. "Steel Meridian".

group.description: faction: the six Relay syndicates with alignments. open-world: syndicates of a hub (Cetus, Fortuna, Necralisk, …). other: Simaris, Conclave, Nightwave, Operational Supply.

alignments.description: Relation to other faction syndicates, keyed by their id. Standing earned here also changes theirs by the fixed game percentage. Must be mirrored in the other syndicate's file.

ranks.description: Every rank in ascending order, including negative ranks of faction syndicates.

standingSources.description: How standing is earned, in short English lines, e.g. "Wear the syndicate sigil", "Cetus bounties".

standingTrades.description: Items handed in for standing (e.g. Entrati family tokens), so the wiki can list them with localized names.

itemName.description: Stand-in for item while filling in: the English name as shown in game.

standing.description: Standing gained per unit handed in.

vendor.description: id of the file in data/vendors/ that takes the trade-in, when known.

title.description: Rank title as shown in game (English), e.g. "Neutral", "Agent".

maxStanding.description: Standing cap while at this rank.

rankUp.description: What it takes to reach this rank from the one below.

cost.description: Everything handed over together: credits, standing, resources or items (by uniqueName).

tasks.description: Non-item requirements, in short English lines, e.g. "Complete a Narmer bounty".
